So how can we get out of the real world? Speaker 1 | 00:24 - 00:33 I'd be really disappointed if we fast forward even five years' time. Like, the predictive understanding of disease biology has not step changed in, like, a massive way. Speaker 2 | 00:33 - 01:07 Do you have a prediction on when you think, for example, eighty percent of human cancers will be treatable? Today, know priors were joined by Max Jadberg. Max is the president and part of the founding team of Isomorphic Labs. Isomorphic is backed by Alphabet and a variety of other investors, and its goal is to solve all disease, which is very exciting as a topic. We're going to talk a little bit about the role of AI in the future of biopharma, human health, longevity. Speaker 2 | 01:07 - 01:22 And Max, of course, has a background in machine learning. He has a PhD in the topic working on machine vision. Eventually sold a company to Google DeepMind, rose up the ranks there, and now is president of isomorphic. Isomorphic, I think, is is one of the more fascinating companies right now that's happening in technology in general. Alphabet is a major shareholder and sort of sponsor.
